title: Quebec's popular PEQ program is closed — again. People counting on it want answers
summary: The popular immigration pathway known as the PEQ was temporarily revived earlier this year. The first period for applications was open between July 2 and Oct. 31, and it's not clear when the Quebec…

image.caption: This protest took place on Nov. 17, 2025, in Montreal as people gathered to denounce the plan to scrap the Programme de l'expérience québécoise, also known as the PEQ program. (Samir Bendjafer/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Montreal·New

The popular immigration pathway known as the PEQ was temporarily revived earlier this year. The first period for applications was open between July 2 and Oct. 31, and it's not clear when the Quebec government will open a second window for applicants.
PEQ was revived this year with 1st application window open from July 2 to Oct. 31
Three weeks after the Quebec government ended the first phase of applications for a popular immigration pathway program, there’s no word on when the second will begin.
And for many people hoping to solidify their future in the province, the clock is ticking.
"Their future is at stake," said Sabrina Kouider-Philippon, the vice-president of group called Le Quebec c'est nous aussi, which loosely translates to "We are also part of Quebec."
"Federal work permits are expiring, work permits aren't getting renewed so these people are losing their statuses and their ability to work and support their families."
For years, the Quebec Experience Program, also known as the PEQ, was a fast track to permanent residency.

The former Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ) government scrapped it in November 2025 and replaced it with a new program known as the PSTQ, which has been criticized as a more restricted pathway toward permanent residency.

items: Quebec temporarily revives PEQ immigration pathway, but advocates call it an 'insult'

blocks.text: After much public outcry, the CAQ temporarily revived the PEQ earlier this year with plans to shut it down for good in 2028. A first window for applications opened this year between July 2 and Oct. 31.
“It is therefore no longer possible to present an application through this program,” reads a message on the Quebec government’s website.
“There has been no decision regarding a new period to accept applications.”

Sabrina Kouider-Philippon, a spokesperson for the group Le Quebec c'est nous aussi, says the lack of clarity surrounding the PEQ program takes a mental toll on people hoping to build their lives in the province. (Guillaume Renaud/CBC)
The second window could open any time between now and July 2028. That lack of clarity is unacceptable, according to Kouider-Philippon.
"People can't make any plans for the future with so much uncertainty."
PQ now in charge

What happens next with the PEQ is largely up to the Parti Québécois (PQ) — the sovereignist party that promised the lowest annual limit for permanent immigration out of the five major parties during the election campaign.
The PQ promised to lower the annual limit from 45,000 to 35,000.

items: What's changing in Quebec’s immigration system — and why it's sparking backlash

blocks.text: In a statement, the spokesperson for Quebec's new Immigration Minister Catherine Gentilcore, said the government is committed to offering a "predictable path toward permanent residence to people who fit criteria established by Quebec," referring to French-language skills and their fit in the province's job market.

"The handling of the PEQ has to also take into consideration our ability to take in people and objectives the province has set for immigration, integration and francization," wrote spokesperson Éli Dubois.
A spokesperson for Quebec's immigration minister says there is no planned date for the reopening of the PEQ program after it closed on Oct. 31. (Ivanoh Demers/Radio-Canada)
Ottawa also needs to step up, group says
The spokesperson for Quebec's immigration minister reiterated that there is no planned date to reopen the PEQ program at the moment.
"The reopening of the program this past summer generated a high volume of requests in a short period of time," he wrote.
He said the PQ government's overall immigration plan will be presented before the holidays.
CBC News asked the province's Immigration Ministry how many PEQ applications it received between July 2 and Oct. 31. We're waiting to hear back.
Kouider-Philippon's group is also asking Ottawa to extend work permits for those caught in limbo while the PEQ program is on hold.
Catherine Gentilcore, who became an MNA after winning a byelection in Terrebonne in 2025, is the province's immigration minister under the Parti Québécois government. (Sylvain Roy Roussel/CBC)

In a statement, a spokesperson for Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) said it's working closely with Quebec "to support the province's labour market needs and to facilitate pathways" to permanent residence.

The IRCC spokesperson highlighted measures put in place both by Quebec or Ottawa to prioritize people with expiring work permits for permanent immigration selection as well as provide or extend work permits to people on the verge of being selected.
The work permit measure, however, seems to apply to the PSTQ program.
Quebec’s PEQ program to return temporarily
The battle continues
For Le Quebec c'est nous aussi, reopening the PEQ for a second wave of applications is just the beginning.

The group believes the program should reopen permanently and for anyone who was in Quebec before Nov. 19, 2025 — the end of the PEQ program before the CAQ revived it — should have an opportunity to apply for it.
Kouider-Philippon said many PEQ hopefuls have already given up and moved to other provinces or their country of origin.
Her group is planning some form of action in the coming weeks to raise awareness about this situation.
"We're not stopping any time soon," she said. "They have to know that this fight will continue."
